To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rSV40 vectors efficiently and stably transduce human neurons, and that they protect these cells from HIV-induced toxicity.

(i) rSV40 vectors transduced > 95% of NT2-N efficiently and stably; (ii) NT2-N transduced with SV(AT) and/or SV(RevM) were protected against HIV replication, and this was stable throughout retinoic-acid-induced neuronal differentiation; and (iii) rSV40 transduced neurons might be a practicable means of delivering therapeutic genes to treat neuro-AIDS.
